ai_show_review.summary: Soaring Dark Star, epic Eleven, and powerful jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The set builds from a fiery Turn On Your Lovelight into a soaring Dark Star that segues seamlessly into Saint Stephen → The Eleven. Highlights include an intense Dark Star intro, scorching runs on Morning Dew, and Pigpen’s gritty harp on Good Morning Little School Girl. Overall the performance is tight and jam‑heavy despite minor tape hiss.
ai_show_review.review: On April 13, 1969 at the University of Colorado Ballroom, the Dead delivered a classic early‑'70s adventure that still feels fresh. The first set kicks off with a blistering Turn On Your Lovelight before diving into a soaring Dark Star whose 20‑minute intro showcases Jerry’s thick Allman‑style tone and fiery lead work. The band rides that momentum straight into Saint Stephen and The Eleven, delivering one of the smoothest segues of the era. Morning Dew shines as a showcase for Jerry’s scorching runs while Pigpen’s harmonica on Good Morning Little School Girl adds gritty texture. Though the tape has a little hiss and occasional drops (the Alligator cut is unfortunate), the Miller soundboard capture is clear, balanced, and arguably the best source for this show. Phil locks into his own musical world, providing a solid bass foundation that interlocks tightly with Mickey and Bill’s drumming, while Bob’s contribution is minimal – fans even joke “Where’s Bobby?” The night ends in a wild jam after an Alligator tease, leaving listeners with a vivid snapshot of the Dead at a creative peak.

best_recording.reason: Excellent Miller soundboard capture – clear, balanced mix with only minor hiss and drops, making it the most complete and listenable version of this show.

key_highlights: Dark Star's 20‑minute Allman‑style intro and extended improvisation
Seamless Saint Stephen → The Eleven transition
Pigpen’s gritty harmonica on Good Morning Little School Girl

band_performance.Jerry: Thick Allman‑style tone, a soaring 20‑minute Dark Star intro and scorching runs on Morning Dew; overall stellar lead work throughout the show.
band_performance.Phil: Immersed in his own musical world, delivering tight bass interplay that locks with the drums during extended jams.
band_performance.Bob: Minimal presence; reviewers note limited guitar/vocal contribution, prompting a tongue‑in‑cheek “Where’s Bobby?” comment.
band_performance.Mickey: Energetic front‑stage hand‑claps during Dark Star and dynamic drumming that drives the improvisations.
band_performance.Billy: Provides tight, supportive drum work that interweaves seamlessly with Mickey throughout the jams.
